items.title: Axis Direct names 35 top stocks to buy; ICICI Bank, HUL and  Maruti Suzuki feature in list
items.description: Corporate India has reported a strong double-digit increase in earnings during the September quarter (Q2 FY27), supported by the fastest aggregate revenue growth in 16 quarters. The growth can be attributed to robust demand for goods and services as the economy sustained momentum despite geopolitical uncertainties and elevated crude oil prices.For a common sample of 3,568 listed companies across industries, aggregate net profit rose 26.2% in the quarter, compared with 15.3% growth a year earlier, according to an ETIG analysis. Revenue increased 22.6% on a low base of 8.2% a year ago.Against the backdrop, Axis Direct in its recent brokerage report has provided stock outlooks across multiple key industry sectors, including cement, banking, pharma, retail and real estate. Here’s the list of the company’s top conviction ideas:

items.title: TVS Motor Company among 4 stocks that close above VWAP
items.description: On November 19, the closing prices of four stocks in the Nifty 500 pack were more than 2% above their respective VWAPs (Volume Weighted Average Prices), according to StockEdge's technical scan data. When the closing price is above the VWAP, it means the stock closed at a price higher than its volume-weighted average traded price during the day. The VWAP gives greater weight to prices at which higher trading volumes occurred.

items.title: Tata Technologies among 4 stocks showing RSI trending up
items.description: On November 20, four Nifty 500 stocks that gained over 6% were highlighted in the RSI Trending Up scan, based on data from StockEdge. An uptrend signal occurs when the RSI value crosses above 50 from below. "RSI trending up" means that the Relative Strength Index (RSI) values are increasing, indicating strengthening momentum in a stock's price. The RSI is a technical indicator commonly used by traders to assess price momentum and trend strength.

items.title: Maruti Suzuki among 6 stocks flashing White Marubozu pattern
items.description: On November 20, six stocks in the Nifty 50 appeared on the ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period and the closing price is the highest.The pattern is represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and little or no lower shadow. It reflects strong upward price movement during the session, with the price moving from the opening level towards the session high by the close. The pattern is commonly studied in technical analysis as an indicator of price momentum.

items.title: India’s stock rally faces valuation test as bond allure grows
items.description: India's stock market is experiencing valuation challenges due to increasing bond yields that diminish equity attractiveness. The gap between government bond yields and stock earnings yield has widened significantly recently. Analysts suggest that high bond yields could hamper valuations as earnings struggle to catch up. Many global firms maintain a bullish outlook on India's market despite this pressure.

items.title: Fairfax raises stake in IIFL Capital to 44.06%
items.description: Fairfax Financial Holdings recently acquired 44 million shares in IIFL Capital for ₹1,540 crore. This transaction occurred immediately after their exit from IIFL Finance. The acquisition of IIFL Capital does not violate any banking license rules. Fairfax is currently engaged in purchasing IDBI Bank, where major stakeholders are divesting their shares. This marks a significant moment in the Indian banking sector with notable cross-border M&A activity.

items.title: NLC India’s energy arm files IPO papers
items.description: NLC India Renewables has submitted its Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) to Sebi for an initial public offering. The IPO will consist of a fresh issuance of equity shares worth up to ₹3,300 crore and an offer for sale. This equity offering aims to raise significant funds for the company's growth initiatives. The proposed IPO combines both new capital and existing share sales by current stakeholders.

items.title: Outward FDI rises 17% to $4.7 billion in October
items.description: Indian companies have made an outward FDI of $4.65 billion in October, up 17.4% from the year-ago period, Reserve Bank of India said Thursday. While India Inc raised its debt-linked investments, there has been a drop in equity investments, data showed. Companies invested $2.05 billion in equities abroad against $2.35 billion a year prior.

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 5 stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty 500 pack, five stocks gained over 7% and their closing prices crossed above their respective 200-day moving averages (DMA) on November 19, 2026, according to StockEdge's technical scan data. The 200-day moving average (DMA) is used by traders as a key indicator for determining the overall trend of a stock. As long as a stock's price remains above its 200-day moving average on the daily timeframe, it is generally interpreted as being in an overall uptrend.

items.title: Sebi, NISM plan capacity-building network for independent directors
items.description: Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey announced plans for a new network to support independent directors' training. The initiative aims to prepare directors for complex issues including financial structures and cybersecurity challenges. This network will encourage peer learning and discussions on boardroom challenges and governance practices. Indian laws mandate independent directors on boards of public companies based on their size and other criteria.

items.title: Paytm, Mobikwik, Pine Labs shares slide on UPI MDR delay report
items.description: Digital payments companies experienced a notable decrease in their share prices on Thursday. Reports suggest that the implementation of merchant discount rate may be postponed beyond the upcoming assembly elections. Paytm parent One97 Communications and One Mobikwik Systems saw drastic drops in their stock values. The news raised concerns about potential delays in monetizing transactions, affecting earnings expectations.

items.title: Weekly Top Picks: These stocks scored 10 on 10 on Stock Reports Plus
items.description: Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, undertakes detailed company analysis for 4,000+ listed stocks. In addition to detailed company analyses, the report also collates analysts’ forecasts and trend analysis for each component. An average score in Stock Reports Plus is calculated by undertaking quantitative analysis of five key investment tools – earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum.

items.title: Stocks in news: Coal India, Paytm, ACME Solar, Jindal Steel, Hexaware Tech and Highway Infra
items.description: Indian equity markets demonstrated a robust recovery after an initial downturn, with benchmark indices bouncing back significantly. The Nifty 50 surged by 286 points, crossing the 25,500 threshold. Attention centered on key players like Coal India and Paytm amidst recent announcements. Firms such as ACME Solar and Jindal Steel also reported progress on critical projects, leading analysts to forecast a positive trend for the index in the near future.

items.title: D-Street braces for gap-down opening on negative GIFT Nifty cues
items.description: Indian equity benchmarks ended higher on Thursday after a recovery from earlier losses during the trading day. The Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex experienced significant gains, primarily due to strong buying interest across key sectors. Auto stocks recorded notable increases of over four percent, leading the market's recovery on that day. Foreign portfolio investors actively bought shares, while domestic institutional investors were net sellers.

items.title: India turns net overweight market for Asia-Pacific fund managers
items.description: India has recently become a net overweight market for fund managers in Asia-Pacific, indicating reduced interest in North Asian equities. The Asia Fund Manager Survey revealed India's net overweight position at 5%, on par with South Korea. Japan continues to be the most favored market among investors, with a net overweight of 38%.

items.title: FPIs pump record Rs 84,291 crore into Indian stocks in first half of November
items.description: In the first half of November, foreign portfolio investors significantly increased their investment in Indian equities. This surge reached ₹84,291 crore, emphasizing the appeal of banking and financial services. A shift in global preferences followed the US midterm elections, which limited investment in other Asian markets. Notably, the Bank Nifty reached lifetime highs, benefiting from this influx.

items.title: Sebi steps up efforts to attract foreign investors, targets 5-day FPI onboarding: Tuhin Kanta Pandey
items.description: Sebi is targeting a reduction in foreign portfolio investor (FPI) onboarding time to five business days as it steps up efforts to attract overseas capital. Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey outlined measures including digitised registration, simplified KYC norms and longer review cycles, aimed at easing compliance and improving access to Indian markets.

items.title: Elara Capital cuts target price for Garden Reach Shipbuilders stock, maintains ‘reduce’ rating; here’s why
items.description: Elara Capital cut its Garden Reach Shipbuilders target price to Rs 2,050, retaining a reduce rating after a 10-month delay in the next-generation corvettes contract impacted revenue and earnings projections.

items.title: Reliance Industries promoters buy 4.26 lakh shares from open market; stock up 14% in 1 month
items.description: Promoter group entities of Reliance Industries bought a combined 4.26 lakh shares through open-market transactions on November 16. The purchases come as RIL shares have rebounded nearly 14% in a month. The stock's recovery follows strong Q2 results and positive brokerage outlook.

items.title: JM Financial hikes target price of Poonawalla Fincorp; sees 24% upside
items.description: JM Financial has raised its target price for Poonawalla Fincorp to Rs 625 from Rs 550, implying an upside of nearly 24% from Rs 503. The brokerage remains bullish on its secured lending strategy, gold loan growth, improving operating efficiency and declining credit costs, while highlighting increasing AI deployment.

items.title: HSBC says Q2 earnings surprised but Q3, Q4 growth likely to slow down; sees this as a bigger downside risk
items.description: HSBC says Indian companies delivered their strongest earnings growth in nearly two years in Q2 FY27, with 67% beating or meeting estimates. However, growth is expected to moderate in the second half. The brokerage sees a sharper consumption slowdown triggered by inflation or El Niño as a bigger downside risk.

items.title: Sebi plans consultation paper to remove FPI constraints absent in other markets
items.description: SEBI is set to release a consultation paper aimed at simplifying regulations for foreign portfolio investors. The goal is to eliminate certain compliance restrictions to enhance India's appeal to global investors. SEBI also plans to expedite the onboarding process, targeting completion in just five business days. Additionally, KYC review cycles for applicable FPIs will be extended, reducing repetitive compliance activities.

items.title: Jefferies’ Chris Wood increases India bet; reduces Taiwan weight as AI stocks walk on thin ice
items.description: Jefferies' Christopher Wood has raised India's weighting in his Asia-Pacific portfolio to 15%, trimming Taiwan exposure as global investors reassess the AI trade. The move comes amid a sharp November rally in Indian equities, record FII inflows and growing interest from global brokerages. With AI stocks facing pressure, is India emerging as an attractive alternative for global investors?

items.title: NSE becomes world’s 5th-largest listed stock exchange, surpasses NASDAQ and HKEX
items.description: NSE has overtaken Nasdaq and Hong Kong's HKEX to become the world's fifth-largest publicly listed stock exchange operator, with a market capitalisation of $59.65 billion. The milestone puts it ahead of global peers and makes it India's ninth-largest listed company, surpassing Kotak Mahindra Bank and LIC in market value.

items.title: Indian finance hub eyes dual share model to kickstart public offers: Report
items.description: Indian regulators are currently assessing a new proposal that would allow companies to introduce dual-class shares for listings in both domestic markets and GIFT City. This initiative seeks to invigorate equity market activity in GIFT City, which has faced challenges regarding limited primary market participation. One class of shares would be traded in rupees, while the other would be dollar-denominated, granting foreign investors easier access alongside reduced tax implications.

items.title: Why did market rally today? Sensex surges 1,500 pts from day's low, Nifty ends above 25,800. 6 Key factors driving the rally
items.description: The Indian stock market has shown impressive gains, with Sensex and Nifty both rising significantly recently. The rupee has strengthened against the US dollar, boosting investor sentiment in the market. Foreign institutional investors continue to purchase Indian equities steadily, reversing previous outflows. Private banking stocks have seen strong purchasing activity, contributing to market growth. Analysts remain optimistic about the overall performance and resilience of the market moving forward.

items.title: SEIL shares rise 3% as BSE clears proposed restructuring agreement with its subsidiary
items.description: Shanti Educational Initiatives (SEIL) shares rose on Friday after BSE issued a no-adverse-observation letter for its proposed restructuring involving its education business and GREW Energy. Under the plan, SEIL will transfer its education business to a subsidiary before merging into GREW Energy, which is proposed to be listed on stock exchanges.

items.title: Manappuram, Muthoot, IIFL Finance shares tumble up to 5% as gold hits 14-month lows. Why is the yellow metal losing its shine?
items.description: Shares of Muthoot Finance, Manappuram Finance and IIFL Finance fell on Friday as gold prices plunged to a 14-month low amid rising expectations of US Fed rate hikes and a stronger dollar. What is driving the sharp correction in bullion, how could it affect gold loan demand, and what lies ahead?

items.title: Sensex jumps 500 points, Nifty above 25,650 as rupee hits 7-month high, FII shopping spree continues. What lies ahead?
items.description: The Indian stock market recorded significant gains with the Sensex and Nifty indexes rising notably. IT stocks led the gains on the Sensex, while some sectors faced losses. Despite fluctuations in broader markets, foreign institutional investors continued to show strong buying interest. Analysts expect the market to remain resilient due to impressive corporate earnings and sustained foreign investments.

items.title: Anthropic shares close 17% higher on first day of trading amid protest, arrests outside Nasdaq
items.description: U.S. stocks plunged on Thursday as a promising open gave way to broad selling, fueled by worries over further Federal Reserve rate hikes. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1,101.11 points, or 2.19 percent, to 49,097.06, closing below 50,000 for the first time since early June. The S and P 500 shed 147.80 points, or 2.02 percent, to 7,175.83, falling for a sixth consecutive session, its longest losing streak since April 2024. The Nasdaq Composite Index dropped 550.69 points, or 2.25 percent, to 23,879.20. All 11 primary S and P 500 sectors ended lower, with consumer discretionary and health care posting the steepest declines. Anthropic surged 17.07 percent in its Nasdaq debut after pricing the largest initial public offering on record at 83 U.S. dollars a share, opening at 111.5 dollars before paring gains. Meanwhile on Thursday (November 19), Police arrested several protesters outside the Nasdaq building in New York City as artificial intelligence company Anthropic began trading following its initial public offering.

items.title: TCS, Infosys, other Indian IT stocks rally up to 4% amid global AI rout despite Anthropic's blockbuster listing
items.description: IT stocks rallied up to 4% despite a global sell-off in AI-linked shares, as investors assessed the impact of Anthropic's blockbuster debut and mounting concerns over the technology sector. Jefferies flagged improving growth but cautioned that the sector recovery remains uneven.

items.title: Tips Films shares rally 16% as firm proposes voluntary delisting from NSE, BSE. What happens to 8,300 shareholders' money?
items.description: Tips Films shares surged on Friday after promoters proposed voluntarily delisting the company from NSE and BSE, seeking to acquire the 25% stake held by public shareholders. The move could offer nearly 8,300 shareholders an exit opportunity. Here's how the delisting process works and how the exit price will be determined.

items.title: Stock picks of the week: 5 stocks with consistent score improvement and upside potential of up to 30% in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: As an investor, if you intend to buy into the market at this point of time, closely watch the sectors that stand to gain the most if oil prices stay lower, or even fall further from current levels.

items.title: Sebi proposes easing additional disclosure norms for foreign portfolio investors
items.description: SEBI has proposed easing additional disclosure requirements for foreign portfolio investors, aiming to improve India's investment climate. The review seeks to align beneficial ownership norms with global standards while retaining safeguards against financial crimes.

items.title: Sebi proposes limiting tenure of chief executives, independent directors at exchanges
items.description: India's Securities and Exchange Board is proposing crucial adjustments to governance norms affecting market institutions. Key suggestions include lowering the age threshold for public interest directors from 75 to 70 years, instituting a maximum of two three-year terms for directors, and restricting managing directors to an eight-year tenure. Current executives can finish their ongoing terms despite these proposed changes. SEBI is seeking public feedback on these recommendations by December 11.

items.title: Trent loses Sensex seat to Shriram Finance in index reshuffle; changes kick in December 21
items.description: Shriram Finance is scheduled to enter the BSE Sensex index from December 21, 2026, replacing Trent. This change is part of a broader reconstitution of several key BSE equity indices announced recently. Significant alterations will also occur within BSE 100 and BSE Sensex Next 50, with multiple stock replacements. Additionally, the BSE BANKEX will remain unchanged during this review period.

items.title: HSBC initiates 'buy' coverage for OnEMI Tech stock, sees 47% upside; check why it's bullish and downside risks
items.description: HSBC initiated a buy rating on OnEMI Technology with a Rs 500 target price, implying 47% upside. Strong AUM growth, digital lending efficiencies and improving credit costs could drive 60% profit CAGR through FY29.

items.title: Market wrap: Apollo Hospital, Axis Bank, Titan Company, Tata Steel top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Friday
items.description: Indian stock markets rallied as the Nifty gained 1.12% and Sensex rose 1.08%, driven by record-breaking private bank stocks. Foreign investor interest in lenders supported gains despite technology-led weakness across Asian markets.
